questions.question: After configuring a WLAN, your users complain that they do not see the SSID. What could be wrong?
choices: Radio Policy is configured to all.

correct.explanation: If the WLAN status is disabled (admin down), clients will not see or join the SSID regardless of other settings.

incorrect.explanation: SSID beaconing enabled is required for visibility — this choice says it is already enabled, so it is not the problem described.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Picking a healthy setting as the fault
incorrect.whatItDoes: SSID beaconing is enabled. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", Status is disabled. satisfies what this question tests — SSID beaconing is enabled. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Multicast settings affect delivery of multicast traffic — they do not typically hide the SSID from clients.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Multicast support is disabled. gives a broadcast or multicast MAC pattern that may not be the all-ones form tested here.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", Status is disabled. satisfies what this question tests — Multicast support is disabled. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Radio policy set to all bands should still advertise the SSID — disabled WLAN status is the direct block.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Over-focusing on band policy when the WLAN is admin-down
incorrect.whatItDoes: Radio Policy is configured to all. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", Status is disabled. satisfies what this question tests — Radio Policy is configured to all. does not.

answerReview.examTip: SSID not visible → check WLAN enabled status first, then beacon/hide SSID settings.

questions.question: How many pre-shared keys can be configured for a specific WPA2 WLAN?
choices: One PSK (one hex or one ASCII)
Two PSKs (one hex and one ASCII)
Four PSKs (two hex and two ASCII)

correct.explanation: WPA2-PSK WLANs use one PSK per SSID (hex or ASCII passphrase) — not multiple concurrent keys.

incorrect.explanation: Cisco WLC does not assign separate hex and ASCII PSKs simultaneously for one WLAN.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Two PSKs (one hex and one ASCII) points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", One PSK (one hex or one ASCII) satisfies what this question tests — Two PSKs (one hex and one ASCII) does not.

incorrect.explanation: Four PSKs is not standard WPA2-PSK personal — one shared key per WLAN.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Four PSKs (two hex and two ASCII) points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", One PSK (one hex or one ASCII) satisfies what this question tests — Four PSKs (two hex and two ASCII) does not.

incorrect.explanation: PSK count is limited — enterprise uses 802.1X, not unlimited PSKs.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Unlimited number of PSKs points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", One PSK (one hex or one ASCII) satisfies what this question tests — Unlimited number of PSKs does not.

answerReview.examTip: WPA2 personal = one PSK per SSID. Enterprise = 802.1X/RADIUS.

questions.question: You are configuring a WPA2 WLAN. Which security configuration should you use for the highest level of security?

correct.explanation: WPA2 with AES (CCMP) is the strongest common WPA2 cipher — avoid TKIP/RC4 legacy options.

incorrect.explanation: WPA-AES is first-generation WPA — WPA2-AES is the stronger, current standard for new deployments.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Stopping at WPA instead of WPA2
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA-AES points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", WPA2-AES satisfies what this question tests — WPA-AES does not.

incorrect.explanation: WPA2-TKIP keeps legacy cipher support — AES/CCMP is stronger and preferred for highest security.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Choosing TKIP under a WPA2 SSID for "security"
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA2-TKIP selects a weak or deprecated WLAN security option.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: WLAN security (wlc gui wlan): WPA2-AES meets the security requirement — WPA2-TKIP is deprecated or too weak for the scenario.

incorrect.explanation: RC4-based options are legacy — WPA2-AES (CCMP) is the exam answer for strongest WPA2 cipher.
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA2-RC4 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", WPA2-AES satisfies what this question tests — WPA2-RC4 does not.

answerReview.examTip: Highest WPA2 security → WPA2-AES (CCMP). Disable TKIP when hardening.

questions.question: You are setting up a wireless network for a client. Their requirements are to minimize the infrastructure and support the highest security. Which wireless encryption standard should be configured to satisfy the requirements?

correct.explanation: WPA2-Personal (PSK) minimizes infrastructure — no RADIUS — while still using modern WPA2 security for a small site.

incorrect.explanation: WPA-Enterprise requires RADIUS and more infrastructure — opposite of minimizing backend services.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Choosing enterprise auth when minimal infra is required
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA-Enterprise points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", WPA2-Personal satisfies what this question tests — WPA-Enterprise does not.

incorrect.explanation: WPA3-Enterprise also needs RADIUS and newer hardware — more complex than WPA2-Personal for a minimal setup.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Over-engineering with WPA3-Enterprise for minimal infra
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA3-Enterprise points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", WPA2-Personal satisfies what this question tests — WPA3-Enterprise does not.

incorrect.explanation: Original WPA-Personal is older than WPA2-Personal — the stem asks for modern security with minimal infrastructure.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Reverting to WPA instead of WPA2-Personal
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA-Personal points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "wlc gui wlan", WPA2-Personal satisfies what this question tests — WPA-Personal does not.

answerReview.examTip: Small site, minimal infra, shared key OK → WPA2-Personal. Enterprise/users → WPA2-Enterprise + RADIUS.
